Subject: Discovery recap: tool-calling & structured output requirements

Samir — thanks again for taking time this morning. Quick recap from our discovery call and proposed next steps so we’re aligned. Pulling out the explicit asks we heard from your team.

Pain points
- Downstream systems are failing on inconsistent output from current LLM pipeline (free-form text -> brittle parsers).
- Agents sometimes call external tools with non-deterministic argument formatting; retries and monitoring are difficult.
- Current stack (homegrown orchestration + Lambdas + Redis KV cache) doesn’t enforce schema validation at generation time.

Current stack / integrations
- Ingestion -> orchestration service -> LLM endpoint -> post-processing (Python microservices)
- Auth via company SSO; logs stored in Splunk; data retention requirements = 90 days

Success criteria (from you)
1) Deterministic, schema-valid JSON output on >95% of calls for primary use-cases.
2) Clear method for function/tool calling that guarantees argument types and formats (no ad-hoc strings).
3) Low-code validation path so downstream services can accept LLM output without brittle parsing.
4) SLA-ish targets for latency: p50 < 300ms for small requests, and reasonable token-cost profile.

What Redwood can deliver / next steps
- We’ll provide a reference JSON schema and example prompts that bias the model toward strict, typed output (see attached example-schema.json).
- Marissa (SE) will propose an agent workflow that supports explicit function/tool calls and fallback behavior for validation failures.
- Dylan will put together a short config recommendation for batching/quantization to meet your latency/cost targets.
- Schedule: propose a technical deep-dive next week to review schema + run a quick end-to-end demo (30–45 minutes).

Please confirm anything I missed or correct the success criteria above. If that looks right, I’ll schedule the deep-dive Tuesday or Wednesday and Marissa will share the schema draft before the meeting.

Attachments: example-schema.json (application/json, 6 KB)

Thanks,

- The primary use-case is checkout data normalization: product attributes must be returned in a strict schema that downstream fulfillment services consume.
- If schema validation fails we need a clear fallback path: either a deterministic retry (with enforced tool-call to our enrichment API) or a human-in-the-loop flag.
- We’ll want example payload sizes: typical calls are ~40–120 tokens output, occasional 400+ tokens for edge cases.

Samir — thanks for the quick confirm. I put together a short technical note and an example schema attached; highlights below. I’ll send the full schema as a separate attachment (example-schema.json) and keep it lightweight for review.

High-level approach (proposal)
1) Prompt + structured output: use a tightly constrained system/prompt layer that instructs the model to only emit JSON matching a provided JSON Schema.
   - We recommend validating the model output against the schema server-side (fail-fast) and classifying failures into deterministic retry vs human triage.
2) Agent/tool calling workflow: explicit function calling semantics (tool: enrich_product, args: {sku: string, attributes: object})
   - All tool calls must use strict typed args. Redwood’s runtime will serialize args as JSON and validate before invoking external APIs.
3) Deterministic formatting success criteria (examples we can measure)
   - Schema pass rate >= 95% on first-generation.
   - When failing, validation error should be classifiable into: (a) missing field, (b) wrong type, (c) malformed JSON.
   - Recovery paths: auto-retry with augmented prompt (include failing example + expected schema) up to N=2, after which send to human queue.

Example minimal JSON Schema (high-level snippet)
{
  "type": "object",
  "required": ["sku", "name", "attributes"],
  "properties": {
    "sku": { "type": "string" },
    "name": { "type": "string" },
    "attributes": {
      "type": "object",
      "properties": {
        "color": { "type": "string" },
        "size": { "type": "string" },
        "weight_kg": { "type": "number" }
      },
      "additionalProperties": false
    }
  }
}

Operational notes
- We’ll include schema examples in the attachment and provide a set of guarded prompts that bias the generator toward strict output.
- For latency/cost tradeoffs we suggest using a smaller quantized model for schema-only calls and a larger model for complex enrichment (tool calls) where semantic reasoning is required.
- Logging: each generation has a validation result (pass/fail + error code) and the runtime emits structured logs to your Splunk endpoint for auditing.

Next steps (technical)
- I’ll share the full example-schema.json (attached).
- Jordan: propose two 45-minute slots Tue/Wed afternoon PT and I’ll own the deep-dive agenda (schema, demo, failure modes, runtime config).
- Dylan: can you draft the batching/throughput notes?
